In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the β-carbon of the surface active lecitiin is the site of the most rapid and extensive change with development, and this change is largely the result of the biosynthetic pathway of the surface active fraction of alveolar lecitin.
the β-carbon of surface active lechitin is largely saturated with palmitic acid, and this saturation is a result of a marked increase in α- to β-palmitoyl transacylation in the developing fetus.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the β-carbon of lecithinic acids are highly saturated (70%) in surface acitve lecithins and are largely palmitic acid.
in fetal lung the biosynthesis of lecithine is by the CDP-choline pathway, and that after the onset of breathing there is a shift to the CDP-ethanolamine pathway.

the biosynthetic pathway for surface active lecthins is the CDP-choline + α-β diglyceride pathway and that the trimethylation pathway is a minor pathway for the biosynthesis of lung surface active lecethins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the α-carbon fatty acids in lecithin do not change significantly with age or with the presence or absence of surface activity.
the α- and the β-carbon of the fatty acid chains of lecithines have very different properties and are involved in the formation of different lecithines.
the surface active lecthins are synthesized in the lung, not in the plasma.
